title: Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the requirement in paragraph 2.e that a multi-site session eventually particularize a site, and struck that provision from the Presbytery Manual.
first_summary: Hope Community Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s policy requiring a multi-site congregation eventually to particularize its second worship site. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled the requirement because BCO 12-5e commits authority over the time and place of worship to the Session, which Presbytery’s general church-enlargement power could not supersede. The provision was stricken from the Presbytery Manual.
summary: Hope Community Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s requirement that a multi-site congregation eventually particularize its second worship site. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the requirement, and struck it from the Presbytery Manual because BCO 12-5e specifically entrusts the time and place of worship to the Session, which Presbytery’s general church-enlargement authority could not supersede. The narrow ruling did not resolve broader concerns about multi-site churches or eliminate Presbytery’s review of a second site’s location under BCO 13-9(g).

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption identifies Case 2013-04 as the Session’s complaint against Central Carolina Presbytery; the SJC adopted the amended opinion 19–0 among members voting (lines 13, 86–90; printed pp. 560, 564).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged paragraph 2.e’s mandate that a multi-site session eventually particularize a site (lines 27–37, 41–49; printed pp. 561–562).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled and struck the requirement, holding that Presbytery’s general BCO 13-9(g) power could not override the Session’s specific BCO 12-5e authority (lines 51–74; printed pp. 562–563).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The decision preserved Presbytery review of the second site’s location and did not decide broader biblical, theological, or polity objections to multi-site structures (lines 63, 76–82; printed pp. 563–564).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. The CCB advice discussed in the record was nonbinding, and the SJC merely recommended reconsideration of a separate manual provision misstating it (line 78; printed p. 563).
